raw_response:
I would keep the farm simple and steady this year because I have 22.5 mu, I have well irrigation, and my household labor is limited since some family members work off-farm. I would put my best land into the wheat-maize rotation because that is my main system and the most reliable way for me to keep grain output stable. I would use improved or hybrid seed where it gives me a clear yield advantage, but I would not push fertilizer to extremes because I want dependable returns, not unnecessary cost. On the 12 mu under wheat-maize, I would manage wheat with enough fertilizer and three irrigations to secure tillering, jointing, and grain filling, then I would follow with no-tillage summer maize to save labor and hold moisture. On the remaining 10.5 mu, I would spread risk across cotton, peanut, millet, and mung bean. Cotton and peanut would take more of that land because they give me cash and fit my experience, while millet and mung bean would stay smaller because they need less input and help me avoid putting everything into one crop. I would use rotary tillage on the spring-sown dryland crops, keep irrigation for the crops that respond best, and use moderate pesticide sprays only to protect yield when pressure is likely.
